assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced proximity as a chemical design principle: bifunctional PROTACs and molecular glue degraders hijack the ubiquitin-proteasome system to remove proteins rather than inhibit them. It opens targets once considered undruggable and has become a general platform across chemical biology and medicinal chemistry, which is the kind of discovery that changes what chemists and clinicians can do.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and first demonstrated the PROTAC concept; Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target underpins the molecular-glue branch. Ciulli, Gray and others made decisive later contributions (VHL ligands, structural rationale, degrader design), so the three-person configuration omits real contributors and the glue/PROTAC split is an open credit question.
assessment.maturity: Many degraders are in clinical trials, with the first Phase 3 readouts emerging, and the mechanism is confirmed independently across many labs and E3 ligases. Timing looks good, though the approved-drug record is still thin.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should centre on PROTACs (Crews, Deshaies) or molecular glues (Handa, Ito) or on both, as I recall the history and have not verified it.
Clinical benefit of degraders is not yet fully established; I cannot confirm trial outcomes.
Credit for Ciulli, Gray and Sakamoto may be contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the enabling delivery chemistry for siRNA therapeutics and mRNA vaccines, a rare case where molecular design (pKa-tuned lipids, microfluidic self-assembly) directly reached billions of people. Impact on medicine and nanomaterials is enormous and obvious.
assessment.attribution: Cullis and colleagues (Hope, Madden, MacLachlan) developed the lipid nanoparticle and ionizable-lipid technology; Anderson and Langer contributed lipidomics and combinatorial lipid discovery. Credit is spread across Vancouver, MIT and industry groups, and the 2023 Medicine prize to Karikó and Weissman for nucleoside modification complicates how the delivery half would be framed.
assessment.maturity: Clinically proven at scale (Onpattro, COVID-19 vaccines) and independently confirmed. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Which of Cullis, Hope, MacLachlan, Madden, Anderson and Langer made the decisive ionizable-lipid contributions is unresolved.
Overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize may count against it; the question is whether it is a distinct chemical discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts one base pair to another without double-strand breaks by fusing deaminases to Cas proteins, using chemical reasoning about nucleobase reactivity. It is a general, precise tool for biology and is now entering therapies.
assessment.attribution: David R. Liu is the clear intellectual driver, with Komor and Gaudelli as lead trainee inventors. Nishida and Kondo (Target-AID) reported a parallel route, so a sole-laureate prize is defensible but not fully uncontested. Ranking this entry rather than prime editing (B017) avoids splitting the same laureate and reflects the longer track record.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted and independently reproduced, with early clinical applications. Because CRISPR was recognized in 2020, there is some question whether this is a distinct prize or a continuation.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would prefer base editing, prime editing or both, and whether Komor and Gaudelli should share.
Clinical durability and safety data are still limited as far as I know.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reassigning codons so that cells incorporate unnatural amino acids gives chemists site-specific control over protein chemistry in living systems. It underpins probes, photocrosslinkers, biologics engineering and orthogonal translation, all of which I use or see in biomaterials work.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang established the first orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs for eukaryotes and bacteria; Chin extended the approach to eukaryotic cells and animals, quadruplet codons and orthogonal ribosomes. Yokoyama and Mehl also made notable contributions, so three is a fair but trimmed set.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed for two decades with broad adoption. Therapeutic uses exist, so recognition is fully mature.
uncertainties: Relative weight of Schultz, Chin and Wang may be disputed.
Some of the field's biggest payoffs (for example, engineered protein drugs) remain partly in development.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Electrical reading of single nucleic-acid molecules through nanopores turned a physical-chemistry idea into commercial long-read sequencing and a platform for single-molecule analytics. It is a strong example of a measurement principle that changed what researchers and clinicians can do.
assessment.attribution: Branton and Deamer proposed the concept, Akeson demonstrated strand translocation and enzyme-controlled movement, and Bayley engineered protein pores. Kasianowicz showed early single-strand detection. Several people could be argued as decisive, and I am unsure of Bayley's current status, which affects how the credit works.
assessment.maturity: Commercially deployed and independently validated, with a sustained record of use. Timely.
uncertainties: Attribution among five or more contributors is hard to settle fairly.
Whether the committee views the prize as chemistry rather than biophysics or sequencing technology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Sequencing-by-synthesis with reversible terminator chemistry and single-molecule detection created the next-generation sequencing that now drives genomics and clinical diagnostics. The key advance is chemical (reversible terminators, fluorescent nucleotides).
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman invented the Solexa chemistry that became Illumina; Rothberg's 454 pyrosequencing and Mayer's colony approach are parallel inventions. A two-person Cambridge prize is cleanest, but Rothberg's claim complicates it.
assessment.maturity: Established and transformative, with decades of use. Recognition would be timely or late.
uncertainties: Competition between multiple technology lineages for the main credit.
Possible view that sequencing sits better under Medicine or Physiology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Shokat showed that mutant KRAS(G12C) can be covalently targeted through a switch-II pocket, turning a notorious undruggable oncogene into a drug target. Chemical-genetic analog-sensitive kinase work added a general tool. This is a clear case of chemical design changing clinical practice.
assessment.attribution: A single-laureate configuration is natural, as the KRAS covalent strategy came from his group, though later optimization by industry (Amgen, Mirati) delivered drugs. Chemical genetics of kinases may be a separate contribution.
assessment.maturity: Sotorasib and adagrasib are approved, so the concept is confirmed, but long-term clinical impact and resistance remain in flux.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as a single discovery or two (kinase chemical genetics and KRAS).
Durability of clinical responses remains incompletely understood to me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Scaffolded DNA origami gave programmable nanoscale construction from a molecule's sequence, with uses in biosensing, drug delivery, plasmonics and molecular machines. It resonates strongly with my interest in molecular design principles for assembly.
assessment.attribution: Rothemund introduced the origami method; Yan and Shih extended it to 3D and complex architectures; Yin and Winfree add other lines. Seeman is the founder of the field but is not among the credited names, which makes the set awkward.
assessment.maturity: Highly cited and reproduced, though real-world applications are still mostly emerging. Somewhat early for Nobel-level translational impact.
uncertainties: Absence of Nadrian Seeman's foundational DNA nanotechnology from the credited names complicates fairness.
Practical impact beyond the lab is still limited.
